systemArchitecture.evolutionPath: can migrate to microservices at scale (100K+ users)

majorComponents.name: User Service
majorComponents.responsibility: Authentication, user profiles, sports preferences, account management

majorComponents.name: Team Service
majorComponents.responsibility: Team creation, membership management, invitations, roster coordination

majorComponents.name: Match Service
majorComponents.responsibility: Challenge creation, match scheduling, score tracking, result verification

majorComponents.name: Stats Service
majorComponents.responsibility: Statistics aggregation, leaderboards, performance analytics, rankings

majorComponents.name: League Service
majorComponents.responsibility: League creation, season management, standings calculation

majorComponents.name: Tournament Service
majorComponents.responsibility: Tournament creation, bracket generation, tournament progression

systemArchitecture.communicationPattern: In-process function calls (monolith), REST-ready interfaces for future extraction
systemArchitecture.deploymentModel: Single container (Docker Compose for local, single EC2/container for production)

technologyStack.authentication: JWT with Passport.js (bcrypt for password hashing)
technologyStack.testing: Jest with TDD workflow (unit, integration, e2e, regression, performance tests)
technologyStack.infrastructure: Docker Compose (local development), AWS ECS or Railway (production)

dataArchitecture.approach: Relational with clear service boundaries for future extraction
dataArchitecture.relationships: User → Teams (many-to-many via team_members), User → Sports (many-to-many via user_sports), Team → Matches (one-to-many), Match → Stats (one-to-one aggregation), League → Teams (many-to-many), Tournament → Matches (one-to-many with bracket structure)
keyPatterns: Soft deletes (is_active flag) for users and teams
Audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at) on all tables
UUID primary keys for all entities
JSON columns for flexible metadata (match_metadata, tournament_bracket)
Materialized views for leaderboards and rankings (future optimization)

performance.apiResponseTime: <100ms for standard CRUD queries, <500ms for aggregations/stats
performance.scalability: Designed for 10K+ users, can scale horizontally to 100K+ with database optimization

security.authentication: JWT with 7-day expiration, bcrypt password hashing (12 rounds), refresh token support
security.dataPrivacy: Field-level access control (own profile shows all fields, other users' profiles hide email/phone), password_hash never exposed in API responses
security.apiSecurity: Rate limiting (100 req/min per IP), Zod input validation on all endpoints, CORS configuration, SQL injection prevention via parameterized queries

quality.methodology: TDD (write tests first) - comprehensive test suite with unit, integration, e2e, regression, and performance tests
quality.errorHandling: Centralized error handling middleware with consistent error response format
quality.monitoring: Structured logging with Winston (future: APM with DataDog or New Relic)

availability.uptime: Best effort for MVP (no SLA), target 99.5% uptime for production
availability.disasterRecovery: Daily automated PostgreSQL backups, 24-hour RPO/RTO acceptable for MVP

developmentStrategy.parallelizationReadiness: Design for eventual parallelization, START SEQUENTIAL for foundation. User Service and Team Service must be stable before parallel development begins. Once base services have 90%+ test coverage and stable interfaces, controlled parallelization (2-3 streams) is safe.
developmentStrategy.serviceIsolation: Clear service boundaries with dedicated folders (services/user-service/, services/team-service/). Each service owns its controllers, routes, repositories, and schemas. Shared utilities in shared/ folder. Design interfaces as if services will be extracted to microservices later (dependency injection, no tight coupling).
developmentStrategy.testingStrategy: Comprehensive test suite to enable confident parallel work. All services must have 90%+ coverage before parallelization. Integration tests act as contracts between services. Test database isolation (separate DB per test suite). Performance tests for critical paths.
developmentStrategy.criticalPathGuidance: CRITICAL PATH: User Service (auth + profiles) → Team Service → Match Service. Stats, League, and Tournament services are non-critical and can be parallelized after Match Service is stable. DO NOT parallelize User and Team services - they are foundational dependencies.
developmentStrategy.technicalDebtPolicy: Refactor immediately if technical debt blocks parallelization or violates 90% coverage target. Track non-blocking debt in GitHub issues. Zero tolerance for security debt (auth vulnerabilities, SQL injection, exposed secrets).

integrationPoints.name: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
integrationPoints.purpose: Push notifications for match updates, challenge invitations, team invites
integrationPoints.fallbackStrategy: Degrade to email notifications if FCM unavailable

integrationPoints.name: AWS S3 / Cloudinary
integrationPoints.purpose: Media storage for user avatars, team logos, match highlight videos
integrationPoints.fallbackStrategy: Use default avatars, skip video uploads if unavailable

integrationPoints.name: SendGrid / Mailgun
integrationPoints.fallbackStrategy: Queue emails for retry, critical for password reset flow

integrationPoints.name: Stripe
integrationPoints.purpose: Payment processing for premium features, tournament fees (future Phase 4+)
integrationPoints.fallbackStrategy: Not critical for MVP, can be added later

constraints.budget: Minimal infrastructure budget - prioritize cost-effective solutions
technical: Must work locally with Docker Compose (zero cloud dependency for development)
Must support multiple sports (pickleball, paddle, basketball, soccer, cricket)
Must be mobile-first (React Native), web admin panel for management

unstructuredNotes:
PM Agent: The architecture prioritizes SEQUENTIAL FOUNDATION BUILDING first - do NOT parallelize User Service and Team Service development. These are critical dependencies and must be rock-solid before moving forward.

Key Architectural Decisions:
1. Chose modular-monolith over microservices: Simpler deployment, faster iteration, can extract services later if needed.
2. Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB: Relational data model fits sports/teams/matches well, complex queries needed for leaderboards/stats.
3. Chose JWT over session-based auth: Stateless, mobile-friendly, easier to scale horizontally.
4. Chose TDD with 90% coverage: High coverage enables confident refactoring and parallel development later.

Critical Risks:
1. N+1 query problem: User → user_sports JOIN can be expensive. Consider eager loading or dataloader pattern.
2. Match result disputes: Business logic needed for verification flow (both teams must confirm results).
3. Leaderboard performance: Denormalize stats or use Redis sorted sets for real-time rankings.
4. Video storage costs: S3 can get expensive. Consider usage limits or compression strategies.

Phase Guidance for PM Agent:
- Phase 1 (Sequential): User Service foundation - auth, profiles, sports preferences. MUST be 90%+ coverage.
- Phase 2 (Sequential): Team Service - build on stable User Service. MUST be 90%+ coverage.
- Phase 3 (Controlled Parallel): Match Service + React Native UI can start in parallel (2 streams).
- Phase 4 (Full Parallel): Stats, League, Tournament services can all be developed independently by multiple agents.

The PM Agent should define MATURITY GATES at end of each phase:
- Phase 1 Gate: All User Service tests pass, 90%+ coverage, JWT working, no auth vulnerabilities.
- Phase 2 Gate: All Team Service tests pass, 90%+ coverage, invitation flow working, integration tests with User Service passing.
- Phase 3 Gate: Match lifecycle complete, mobile app can create/view matches, integration tests passing.

Security Note: Password reset flow is critical - include in early phases. Focus on registration, login, token refresh, and password reset as core auth features.

Performance Note: Redis is included in stack for session management and rate limiting initially. In later phases, use Redis sorted sets for leaderboards to avoid expensive SQL aggregations.
